svg.title: The xz-utils backdoor: what was in Git versus what shipped in the release tarball
svg.desc: Two panels compare the public Git tree with the release tarball for xz-utils 5.6.0 and 5.6.1. Both contained the payload-carrying test fixtures tests/files/bad-3-corrupt_lzma2.xz and tests/files/good-large_compressed.lzma, committed openly and disguised as corrupt-input test data. The Git tree contained a benign m4/build-to-host.m4. The release tarball contained a modified m4/build-to-host.m4 that existed nowhere in Git. That one file is the divergence. A four-step chain follows: configure runs the modified macro, a sed pipeline extracts the staged script from the test fixture, the script patches liblzma during compilation on glibc x86-64 RPM and DEB packaging builds only, and distribution-patched sshd reaches the backdoor because it links libsystemd which pulls in liblzma. A footer states that the account operating as Jia Tan was not a stolen account but one that earned commit and release-manager rights over roughly two years, and that comparing the tarball against the Git tree would have exposed the single divergent file.
svg.text: xz-utils 5.6.0 / 5.6.1: the divergence was one file
The payload sat in Git in plain sight. What shipped only in the tarball was the code that switched it on.
present — committed openly, disguised as corrupt-input test data
present — the second stage of the same payload
benign. Nothing here reads or executes those test files.
MODIFIED — this version exists nowhere in Git.
What that one file set in motion at build time
A sed pipeline pulls the staged
script out of the test fixture.
Only on glibc x86-64, and only
on RPM or DEB packaging builds.
The account operating as “Jia Tan” was not stolen. It contributed for roughly two years, earned commit access, then release-manager rights,
and used that standing to publish tarballs nobody diffed against the tree. Upstream OpenSSH does not link liblzma; the exposure came from distribution patches.
A build that produced the tarball from the tagged commit, and published provenance saying so, would have made the single divergent file visible.
